yt.title: Your card's last digit catches {c_single} of one-digit typos #Shorts
yt.description:
Luhn mod-10 check digit (ISO/IEC 7812-1). We generated 2,000 random 16-digit test numbers with valid check digits, then tried every single-digit substitution (detected: {c_single}) and every swap of two different neighboring digits (detected: {c_trans}; 09 <-> 90 is the classic miss). No real card numbers were used.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: The last digit is a checksum
scenes.narration: The last digit of a payment card number is not random. It is a check digit.
Starting from the right, double every second digit, add up all the digits, and the total must end in zero. That is the Luhn check.

scenes.label: of single-digit typos detected
scenes.narration: We tried every possible one digit typo on two thousand random numbers. The check caught {c_single_say} percent of them, and about {c_trans_say} percent of swapped neighbor digits.
So a form can warn you about a typo instantly, before anything is sent. It does not make a number secret or secure.
